title: Memory safety absolutists
summary: A critical examination of the 'memory safety absolutist' movement in software engineering, arguing that blanket mandates for memory-safe languages miss important trade-offs in systems programming where performance, control, and legacy codebases require nuanced consideration of C/C++ alongside modern alternatives like Rust.
problem_solved: Addresses the oversimplified debate around mandating memory-safe languages without considering performance, control, and practical migration challenges in existing codebases.
why_valuable: Provides a balanced perspective on the memory safety debate, helping developers and decision-makers understand that one-size-fits-all mandates may not serve all use cases, especially in performance-critical and embedded systems.
